cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: the right-tailed F distribution at 15.2068649 with 6 and 4 degrees of freedom
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes '=F.DIST.RT(A2,A3,A4)' over the data 15.2068649 / 6 / 4 with the result 0.01. Re-derived independently with mpmath at 50 decimal digits from the regularized incomplete beta function -- the closed form of the F cumulative distribution, P(F <= x) = I_{d1*x/(d1*x+d2)}(d1/2, d2/2) -- rather than from any statistics library's F routines. The right tail is 1 - P(F <= x) = 0.009999999952464600992, which rounds to exactly the published 0.01 at 8 dp -- the page's x is quoted to enough digits here that the published figure and the derived one agree well past the printed depth, unlike the F.DIST page's 4-decimal x.

cases.description: A negative x, which the documentation excludes
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If x is negative, F.DIST.RT returns the #NUM! error value." EXECUTED RESULT: all four LibreOffice builds (24.2.0.3, 24.8.7.2, 25.2.0.3, 25.8.7.3) return #VALUE! here instead of the documented #NUM! -- the same systemic #VALUE!-substitution pattern already recorded across this corpus, an error-code difference rather than a computation one.
